sentences.text:
Author: K.Suresh Reddy
Bench: K.Suresh Reddy
 Hon'Ble Sri Justice K.Suresh Reddy
 W.P.No. 4100 of 2023
Order:

-
Questioning the action of the 2nd respondent in seizing the Lorry bearing No.AP 39 UF 3389 along with granite slabs belonging to the petitioner as illegal and arbitrary and for a consequential direction to release the said Lorry, the present writ petition is filed.
Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner as well as the learned Government Pleader for Mines and Geology.

It is contended by the learned counsel for the petitioner that the petitioner is the owner of the above said Lorry and on 15-02-2023 the said vehicle was seized by the 2nd respondent and registered a case in Cr.No.31 of 2023 of Martur Police Station for the offence punishable under Section 420 IPC and Section 21(4) of MMDAR Act.
It is alleged in the F.I.R that the petitioner is transporting the granite slaps without obtaining any permission or waybill and clandestinely doing the business in granite slabs.
The 2nd respondent basing on the panchanama, assessed the value of the granite slabs as Rs.1,50,000/-.
The further contention of the learned counsel for the petitioner is that the petitioner is having valid permit, waybill and invoice and the same have been annexed to the present writ petition.
In the invoice, the value of the goods including GST was shown as Rs.2,15,377/-.
Further, the petitioner has also produced e-waybill and transit pass.

He, therefore, requested this court for a direction to the respondents to verify the above invoice, waybill and transit pass and pass appropriate orders with regard to release of the above said Lorry.

Having regard to the above facts and circumstances of the case, this court deems it appropriate to dispose of the writ petition, at the stage of Admission, with the following direction:-
"The respondents, in particular, respondent Nos.2 and 3, are directed to verify the invoice, waybill and transit pass furnished by the petitioner and pass appropriate orders in accordance with the extant Rules with regard to the release of the above said Lorry along with granites within a period of one(1) week from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.

In case, if anything excess is found, the respondent Nos.2 and 3 are at liberty to collect the penalty in terms of Clause(iii) Sub-rule(3) of Rule 26 of Karanam Aswani, vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh, on 21 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/113931322/
1 the Andhra Pradesh Minor Mineral Concession Rules,1966
